findings.text: Global template output escaping is explicitly turned OFF. `server.js:135` calls `swig.setDefaults({ autoescape: false })` — the graph shows the live assignment `_tmp_4.autoescape = false` at server.js:137, with `autoescape: true` present only inside a '/* Fix for A3 - XSS, enable auto escaping */' comment. Swig is the registered view engine for all `.html` views (server.js:116 `app.engine(".html", consolidate.swig)`, :117 `app.set("view engine","html")`), so every `{{ var }}` interpolation in every template renders unescaped. This removes the app's primary, highest-blast-radius XSS defense for all `res.render` sinks, including `res.render("profile", {...doc, environmentalScripts})` (profile.js:33) which spreads whole user-controlled DB documents into the template.

Session cookie is configured without any security attributes. `server.js:78` registers `app.use(session({ secret: cookieSecret, saveUninitialized: true, resave: true }))`. The graph shows exactly three live option assignments — `_tmp_2.secret` (:82), `_tmp_2.saveUninitialized = true` (:84), `_tmp_2.resave = true` (:85) — and NO `cookie` assignment at all: the `cookie: { httpOnly: true /* secure: true */ }` block and the generic `key: "sessionId"` block are both inside /* Fix */ comments. Consequently the session id cookie is served with no httpOnly (readable by any XSS, which autoescape:false makes trivial), no secure flag, no SameSite, and no maxAge, under the default `connect.sid` name. The server is plain HTTP (`http.createServer(app).listen(port)` at server.js:145), so the cookie also transits in cleartext.
